world 0 (key testbed).reader_note: Strains sown in strips beside local wheat and results published gives testbed; seed ordered from the breeder kills wellspring and stopgap (the closed merchant is a lure). Yardstick is a strong near-miss since the station compared strains.

world 1 (key yardstick).reader_note: Yield printed at the head of the report with visits to farms a fifth below decides yardstick; 'one strain ... same methods every year' kills testbed and selling to a flour mill kills wellspring and stopgap.

world 2 (key stopgap).reader_note: Opened after the last seed merchant closed and turned to cattle once a seed company arrived: a stopgap; 'the district's usual wheat' kills testbed, and being the literal seed source makes wellspring a near-fit that misses the temporariness.

world 3 (key wellspring).reader_note: Sacks handed out until nearly every field was sown from them, and the crosses spreading into three counties, decide wellspring; testbed literally fits the crossing work, and stopgap fits filling the gap left by the closed merchant but nothing marks it as temporary.

world 3 (key warehouse).reader_note: Schoolhouse is off topic. The sheds holding shipped-whole cars until dealers called decide warehouse; 'sold cars... since 1930' kills toehold.

world 0 (key toehold).reader_note: Small fenced kit plant before a fortyfold expansion decides toehold; warehouse literally fits the freight yard and crates, managers sent from abroad kill schoolhouse, and the single dealer weakens showroom.

world 2 (key schoolhouse).reader_note: Every engineer and foreman spending two years on its line before running the inland factories decides schoolhouse; toehold is killed because the company already owned two factories, and a few hundred cars a year in a plain shed weakens showroom and warehouse.

world 2 (key smothered).reader_note: Digging through layers to doorways gives smothered; benchmarks at 1880 height kill tilted and submerged (the leaning lighthouse is the literal lure), burial kills scoured.

world 3 (key scoured).reader_note: Bare rock grooved downhill with debris swept offshore decides scoured; the askew breakwater is a literal lure for tilted, but benchmarks at 1880 height kill tilted and submerged, bare rock kills smothered.

world 0 (key submerged).reader_note: 'every benchmark ... sat nine meters lower' (uniform, kills tilted), walls 'still stood' (kills scoured), farms 'planted as before' (kills smothered); anchoring above the village walls nearly hands over submerged, though the island is only partly under water.

world 1 (key tilted).reader_note: The quays under the harbor literally fit submerged, but the eastern caves rising nine meters show one end went up while the other went down; the farms unchanged in between kill smothered and scoured. The reader has to combine east and west.

world 0 (key uncovered).reader_note: Overpaint removed revealing figures beneath gives uncovered; scrubbed literally fits the solvent and the smoke; panels going back as they came out kills transferred.

world 1 (key transferred).reader_note: 'Laid the paint layer ... onto light canvas' nearly defines transferred; leaving the darkened varnish kills uncovered and scrubbed, 'sound oak' kills stabilized.

world 2 (key stabilized).reader_note: 'returned the altarpiece as dark with smoke and varnish as it had arrived' kills both scrubbed and uncovered in one phrase; transferred has no support, leaving stabilized from the wax-and-frame sentence.

world 3 (key scrubbed).reader_note: Strong solvents working into the paint and glazes coming off on the swabs point to overcleaning; uncovered is the near-miss (the varnish was removed) but ignores the damage; 'went back into the frame as they had come out' kills transferred and stabilized.

world 3 (key valve).reader_note: Stores water behind the ice dam then releases it gives valve; the warm July outflow kills thermostat, the release kills sink.

world 0 (key thermostat).reader_note: Cold bottom outlet keeping ponds from freezing or overheating decides thermostat; outflow tracking inflow within a day kills valve and sink, tributary inverts the relation.

world 1 (key tributary).reader_note: The pond-temperature setup lures thermostat, killed by 'leaves as icy in January and as warm in August as the river arrives'; outflow 'a third larger than its inflow' kills sink and makes the lake an added source, and the constant ratio in drought and wet years undercuts valve.

world 2 (key sink).reader_note: Seepage through the limestone, half the inflow out and none in dry summers decide sink; tributary is the reverse; thermostat fails because the shallow lake warms the outflow rather than regulating it; valve is a plausible near-miss but implies control.

world 1 (key saturated).reader_note: Every fish sold the same morning to the same number of buyers, a third going for fertilizer: saturated. The price collapse kills steadied; stifled is the near-miss.

world 2 (key stifled).reader_note: Half the small crews quitting and a single storm leaving nothing to sell decide stifled; that same line kills both saturated and steadied, and uprooted only literally describes crews moving to canneries.

world 3 (key uprooted).reader_note: Boats and buyers moving four miles to the village makes uprooted the precise reading, but the blank's object is 'the city's fish market', which the rule did choke off, so stifled stays defensible; the fleet growing by a third only argues against stifling the trade, not the city's market.

world 0 (key steadied).reader_note: The shops going from daily prices to once-a-season price lists decides steadied; stifled is the near-miss (crews lost their freedom to sell) but buyers came every day; uprooted and saturated have no support.

world 2 (key transplanted).reader_note: Songs carried to the mill cities by records and played there: transplanted. 'Whole and in the old rough style' kills smoothed and stripped; singers leaving kills silenced.

world 3 (key silenced).reader_note: Families stopping singing to listen, few under forty knowing a line, decides silenced; 'every verse and every rough voice' kills stripped and smoothed, transplanted has no movement.

world 0 (key stripped).reader_note: Ballads cut from twenty verses to five or six gives stripped; rough voices and tunings kept 'as the engineers had found them' kills smoothed, porches ringing for decades kills silenced, and songs staying in the region kills transplanted.

world 1 (key smoothed).reader_note: 'Drop the slides and cracks from their voices' with retuning to standard pitch decides smoothed; stripped is the near-miss but is killed by 'still sang every verse', and silenced by singing all over the region.

world 2 (key umbrella).reader_note: Icy bodies absorbed and rocky planets hit twenty times less often gives umbrella; 'hardly any icy body left the system' kills slingshot and the 'ragged inner edge' kills shepherd.

world 3 (key tether).reader_note: Rocky planets 'struck about equally often in both runs' kills umbrella and the belt thinning 'much as it did without the giant' kills slingshot; tether is the near-miss for a swarm held in step, shepherd fits the gathered, co-moving swarm better.

world 0 (key slingshot).reader_note: Icy bodies thrown onto stretched paths and out of the system decide slingshot; umbrella (the familiar Jupiter-as-shield idea) is killed by impacts about as frequent as without the giant; shepherd and tether imply holding bodies in place, but the belt lost half its members.
